traits: Cap 5 to 12 cm, ash-grey, olive or grey-brown, darker at the centre, with radial fibrils, often split at the edge
Gills broad and deep, whitish then cream, nearly free, edges serrated
Stem 5 to 12 cm, fibrous and tough, paler than the cap, with white cords at the base
Thin, whitish flesh; mild to slightly bitter taste, no distinctive smell
Rotting broadleaf wood, also beechnuts in the soil · late spring to autumn
safetyNote: Toxic: the DGfM lists it for a gastrointestinal syndrome, and Wikipedia (fr) says it was eaten in Italy, mixed with other species, despite its bitterness, and is now considered toxic. Wikipedia (fr) names look-alikes among Pluteus cervinus, Hymenopellis radicata and Tricholoma portentosum; the thin flesh, broad soft gills and white cords help set it apart. There is no English page read: the text comes from Wikipedia (fr) and the DGfM.
